Reading Review — Anna Bokhonko

A2 Key for Schools — every wrong question, with the original text and why the correct answer is right.

                                                      Part  Score                                                Wrong
1 — short notices                                             4/6
2 — three texts, matching                                     5/7                                       Q4, Q6
3 — long article                                              5/5                                       Q9, Q13
4 — word-choice cloze                                         5/6                                       — none
5 — open cloze                                                5/6                                       Q24
                                                                                                        Q27

Part 1 — notices

  Q4 — "Concert tickets: Buy these on the school website, then collect them from the office"
  A. Pay for tickets online before picking them up at school ✓ B. Check the website for when tickets are available C. Let the office
  know soon if you plan to buy tickets
  Why A: two-step process — buy online, then collect from office. C invents contacting the office beforehand, which the notice never asks
  for.

  Q6 — "Swimming Competition: To enter the races, you must be able to swim more than 200 metres."
  A. Swimmers at all levels can enter B. This competition is for people who can swim over 200m ✓ C. The races will be 200 metres
  long
  Why B: "swim more than 200m" is a minimum ability requirement to enter — it says nothing about the length of the actual races.

Part 2 — three texts (Amy / Flora / Louisa), garden competition

Amy: "won a prize... flowers all different colours" · Flora: "won second prize... our prize is a visit to a special garden with butterflies" · Louisa: "flowers all
yellow... teacher taught us about the butterflies"

  Q9 Whose class won a trip? chosen: A Amy correct: B Flora ✓
  Why Flora: Amy won a prize too (TV film), but only Flora's prize is specifically a visit/trip.

  Q13 Whose class chose flowers the same colour? chosen: A Amy correct: C Louisa ✓
  Why Louisa — direct contradiction: Louisa's flowers are "all yellow" (one colour). Amy's text says the opposite: "all different colours".
  Worth flagging — picking the exact opposite of what's written means the key adjective got skipped, not just guessed wrong.

Part 4 — "Wivenhoe hotel" word-choice cloze (only 1 wrong)

  Q24 — "the best hotel they have ever ___ at" chosen: A entered correct: B stayed ✓
  Why "stayed": "stay at a hotel" is the fixed phrase for a guest's visit. "Enter at" isn't correct English — you enter a place, no "at".

Part 5 — open cloze (email)

  Q27 — "I heard that a ___ of Canadians speak two languages" written: fact correct: lot ✓
  Why "lot": "a lot of + people" is the quantity phrase the gap needs. "A fact of Canadians" isn't an English phrase — "fact" doesn't take "of
  + people" this way.

Pattern: Anna's mistakes cluster around picking an option that repeats a real word from the text but ignores a small qualifying detail — a
minimum requirement mistaken for a fact (Q6), a "prize" mistaken for a "trip" (Q9), and most tellingly Q13, where she chose the option stating
the opposite of the text. That points to reading fast for the general topic rather than checking the one key word each question hinges on. Q4/
Q24/Q27 are fixed-phrase gaps (pay online before picking up, stay at a hotel, a lot of) — a short collocation drill would help, but Part 1–2
accuracy will likely improve fastest just from slowing down.
